subject: treasureChest
pitch: A pirate's treasure chest with its lid thrown open. Weathered dark wood planks bound with rusty iron straps and studs, a heavy padlock hanging loose, and spilling out of it: gold coins, a pearl necklace, a jewelled goblet and a few red and green gems. A small skull-and-crossbones is carved on the front.
reasoning:
I'm working out the safe parts of the SDK to rely on, since I'm not fully certain of exact signatures—sticking with builder, joint, and part calls, and figuring out how rotation, direction, and scale options are likely named.

For the chest design, I'm planning the hinge geometry for the lid: the box body spans 1.0 wide, 0.6 deep, 0.45 tall, with the hinge at the back top edge and the lid rotating open roughly 110 degrees. I'm computing the rotation manually using the standard X-axis rotation matrix to figure out the opened lid's position in model space.

Now I'm designing the lid itself as a flat slab box topped with a half-cylinder barrel shape to give it a curved profile, plus thin plank-like boxes layered on top for texture, all positioned relative to the hinge point.

I'm writing a helper function that applies a rotation and translation to a geometry before attaching it as a skeletal part, so I can reuse it for building out each piece of the whole figure through the joint hierarchy starting from the chest root.

Now I'm fleshing out the treasure chest body itself—open-top box walls with a dark interior, a gold pile made from a squashed low-poly sphere, and scattered small cylindrical coins spilling over the front edge onto the floor, plus iron strap boxes running down the front.

Working out the curved iron straps on the lid, using partial half-cylinder shells rotated to wrap around the lid's curved surface, calculating the geometry transforms needed to align them properly.

Adding plank seam lines across the lid as thin dark rings, plus an interior box for the lid's underside, and now I'm planning a hasp plate on the front for a hanging padlock detail.

With the lid open, I'm placing the lock's staple loop on the body's front with a hanging lock box and torus shackle engaging it at a slight tilt, then starting a skull carving decoration on the chest's front face.

I'm adding a flattened skull shape with eye sockets, jaw, and crossed bones in dark brown relief against the wood, then iron corner brackets and bands along the body's edges with small feet, plus faint plank seams on the front. Now I'm draping a pearl necklace of tiny spheres along a curved path over the rim and into the treasure pile.

I'll build the pearl strand using a CatmullRom curve with white pearl spheres and a gold clasp, then add a tipped goblet made from a lathe geometry with gold and red gem detailing, positioned leaning into the pile.

For the gems scattered through the pile, I'll use small red and green octahedrons with low detail, placing them randomly using a simple custom random number generator instead of relying on an uncertain rng API, then scatter coins across the pile area using similar randomized positioning.

Now I'm working out the coin pile height formula and spill pattern, with coins spreading over the front edge and down to the floor, some stacked, flattened cylinders colored in two gold tones, keeping the triangle budget manageable across roughly 200 coins. I'm also considering the angle the open lid should rest at.

Writing helper functions for placing geometry with position and rotation matrices, and setting up local-to-world transforms for lid-attached parts via hinge rotation...

Now I'm laying out the body's wall boxes, floor, and interior fill with dark wood tones, and planning alternating plank colors across the front panel.

Adding iron hardware...

Working out the hasp plate's position on the arc and its rotation so its face normal matches the tangent direction at that angle.

Now placing studs along the lid straps at increasing φ increments using the outward radius, adding rear hinge cylinders at the chest hinge line, and sketching out the skull as a scaled sphere positioned at the front.

For the skull details, I'm adding a small jaw box, dark eye sockets, and crossed bone shapes with knobbed ends underneath—choosing a pale bone-like color for the cranium so it contrasts against darker eyes and the wood carving beneath.

I'm now working out positioning so the skull, crossbones, and padlock staple don't overlap, adjusting their y-coordinates and sizes until everything fits cleanly above the floor and straps. Next I'm moving on to building the gold pile using squashed low-poly spheres for the coin mass.

Placing coins algorithmically...

Now for the overall structure I'm setting up joints: a root "chest" bone, with the lid attached via a hinge joint parented to chest, and making sure other parts explicitly reference chest as their bone rather than defaulting to the nearest one.
